sources.title: Roger Temam, Navier–Stokes Equations and Nonlinear Functional Analysis, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: §2.5 Flow in a bounded domain and §3.1 A priori estimates, printed pp. 15–18 (PDF pp. 33–36).

contents.name: §2.5 bounded-domain spaces and fixed-boundary Navier–Stokes formulation
contents.support: Context for the bounded-domain incompressible model. The assigned definition states the forced full residual and matching-trace interface locally.

contents.name: §3.1 smooth-solution energy identity and differential energy estimates
contents.support: Independent energy-estimate treatment. The assigned theorem derives the residual term, boundary cancellation, integrating-factor bound, and explicit channel lift locally.

sources.title: Erik Wiedemann, Lecture Notes: Navier–Stokes Equations
sources.locator: §5.1 periodic relative-energy calculation, printed pp. 38–39 (PDF pp. 37–38); §5.2 bounded-domain weak formulation and Kato boundary-layer criterion, printed pp. 41–43 (PDF pp. 40–42).

contents.name: §5.1.1 periodic relative-energy calculation and Grönwall estimate
contents.support: Independent periodic residual-to-error treatment. Its periodic Leray-projected setting is distinct from the assigned bounded-domain full-momentum residual.

contents.name: §5.2 bounded-domain no-slip test functions and Kato's vanishing-viscosity criterion
contents.support: The complete section identifies the no-slip test-function condition and proves a separate inviscid-limit result via a boundary corrector. The assigned theorem makes no viscosity-uniform inviscid-limit claim.

sources.title: John W. M. Bush, MIT 18.357 Interfacial Phenomena, Chapter 19: Water waves
sources.locator: Chapter 19 Water waves, printed/PDF pp. 78–79, equations (19.1)–(19.4), including the linearized capillary boundary condition and finite-depth dispersion derivation.

contents.name: Linearized capillary-gravity potential problem, vertical profile, and finite-depth dispersion
contents.support: The notes derive the same surface-tension curvature sign, solve the finite-depth harmonic profile, and obtain the factor (gk+sigma*k^3/rho)*tanh(kh). The energy conservation argument is proved locally in the assigned item.

sources.title: ETH Zürich, Mechanics of Continuous Media, lecture 23: Capillary waves
sources.locator: Complete seven-page handwritten lecture, printed pp. 181–187 (PDF pp. 1–7); relevant 'Capillary waves' derivation is printed pp. 185–187 (PDF pp. 5–7).

contents.name: Surface-energy variation, Laplace-pressure sign, and deep-water gravity-capillary dispersion
contents.support: Independent capillary derivation confirms the surface-tension pressure sign and the deep-water sigma*k^3/rho contribution. It does not supply the finite-depth tanh factor or the energy conservation proof.

sources.title: Eric Firing, University of Hawaiʻi OCN 620, chapter 19: Surface waves, Part 1
sources.locator: Complete chapter §§19.1–19.7 read; §19.4 Dispersion relation, especially lines 132–145 in the rendered HTML.

contents.name: §19.4 capillary, combined deep-water gravity-capillary, and finite-depth gravity dispersion formulas
contents.support: Independent course-note context for the capillary and gravity contributions. Its combined formula is the deep-water limit; finite-depth capillary dispersion is established from the linear model and MIT derivation.

per_item.argument: The assigned bounded-domain estimate is proved locally from the full forced momentum residual, matching boundary traces, the C1 divergence theorem, and an integrating factor. Wiedemann's periodic relative-energy inequality is context only; its bounded-domain section concerns the distinct viscosity-to-zero problem and does not supply the assigned wall estimate.
